hook: Twenty-five calculus books, in reading order.

beats.say: From the nineteen-ten classic that promises any fool can do it, to the textbook that makes you prove every single line.
The list runs in steps, starting with five books with almost no prerequisites, then ten more where the real work begins.
Richard Feynman learned calculus at thirteen from a library book, Calculus for the Practical Man, before his school ever reached the subject.
